Diese Erklärung gilt für das Spiel Bacteria Wars unter bacteria-wars.wolsok.de (bisher bacteria-game.wolsok.de) und für die Android-App „Bacteria Wars“ (de.wolsok.bacteriawars). Die Speicherung ist für das Spiel, das du ausdrücklich aufrufst, unbedingt erforderlich (§ 25 Abs. 2 Nr. 2 TDDDG). Du kannst die Daten jederzeit löschen: im Browser, indem du unter „Website-Einstellungen“ die gespeicherten Daten von bacteria-wars.wolsok.de löschst; in der Android-App zusätzlich in den Android-Einstellungen unter Apps → Bacteria Wars → Speicher und Cache → „Speicher löschen“.

Name, E-Mail-Adresse oder andere Angaben zu deiner Person brauchen wir dafür nicht.

Das Gastkonto wird so zu deinem Google-Konto, und dein Fortschritt steht dir auf jedem Gerät zur Verfügung, auf dem du dich anmeldest. Dein Name wird nur dir im Spiel angezeigt; andere Spieler sehen ihn nicht. Für die Anmeldung öffnet das Spiel das Anmeldefenster von Google (accounts.google.com, apis.google.com und die Anmeldeseite des Firebase-Projekts auf firebaseapp.com); dabei erhält Google deine IP-Adresse und Angaben zum Browser. Privacy policy

Last updated: 23 October 2026

This policy covers the game Bacteria Wars at bacteria-wars.wolsok.de (formerly bacteria-game.wolsok.de) and the Android app “Bacteria Wars” (de.wolsok.bacteriawars). In short: the game shows no ads, uses no analytics or tracking and sells no data. It only stores what it needs to keep your progress. When you play the game embedded in another site, such as angularexamples.wolsok.de, this policy does not cover that site and its services. The German version above is the binding one.

1. Controller

Wolfram Sokollek
Email: privacy@wolsok.de

Contact this address with any question about your data or to exercise your rights.

2. Loading the game (hosting)

The game is delivered by Firebase Hosting (provider: Google Ireland Limited, address as in section 4). When you load the game, the servers process your IP address, the date and time, the requested file and details of your browser and operating system, as they need to in order to send you the files. They are served from the closest location of Google's content delivery network. We analyse no access logs.

Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, our legitimate interest in delivering the game securely and quickly. For transfers to the USA see section 4.

3. Storage on your device

The game keeps the following in your browser's or the app's local storage (local storage, IndexedDB, the service worker's cache):

  • your settings (game mode, level, colours, graphics, sound, volume, vibration),
  • your progress (medallions, achievements with their dates, statistics, daily level, best endless run) while you play without a cloud account, otherwise a copy of it for playing offline,
  • the game's own files, so that it runs offline too.

This data does not leave your device except as described in section 4. The game sets no cookies. The storage is strictly necessary for the game you chose to open (§ 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG). You can delete it at any time: in the browser by clearing the stored data of bacteria-wars.wolsok.de in its site settings; for the Android app also in Android's settings under Apps → Bacteria Wars → Storage & cache → “Clear storage”.

4. Progress in the cloud and accounts

So that your progress is not lost, the game can keep it in Google Firebase (Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore; provider: Google Ireland Limited, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland). When this is on, the profile says “Playing as a guest” or “Signed in as …”.

As a guest

On first start the game creates an anonymous guest account. Firebase gives it a random identifier (user ID). Under that identifier we store your progress (medallions, achievements with their dates, statistics, daily level, best endless run) and when it last changed. We need no name, email address or other personal details for that.

Signing in with Google (optional)

If you sign in with Google, Google passes us your name, email address, profile picture (its address) and Google ID. Your guest account becomes your Google account, and your progress is available on every device you sign in on. Your name is shown only to you in the game; other players never see it. To sign in, the game opens Google's sign-in window (accounts.google.com, apis.google.com and the Firebase project's sign-in page on firebaseapp.com), which gives Google your IP address and browser details. Google's privacy policy applies to the sign-in itself.

With every connection Firebase also processes technical data such as your IP address and browser details to provide the service and prevent abuse. Only you can read and change your progress.

Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (providing the game you use). Google processes the data on our behalf. Google LLC is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework; any transfer to the USA relies on the European Commission's adequacy decision (Art. 45 GDPR).

We keep this data for as long as your account exists. Section 8 explains how to have it deleted.

5. Google Fonts

The game loads its fonts and icons from Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com; provider: Google Ireland Limited), which gives Google your IP address and browser details. After the first load the game keeps the fonts in your device's cache. Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, our legitimate interest in a consistent, readable look. See the Google Fonts privacy FAQ.

6. Android app

The Android app is a Trusted Web Activity: it opens the game at bacteria-wars.wolsok.de fullscreen in Google Chrome (or another browser on your device). Without a suitable browser, the app shows the game in Android's built-in WebView. The app itself collects no data and asks for no permission to your location, contacts, camera, microphone or files. Everything above about the game in the browser applies. The browser's own privacy policy applies to the browser. Google Play handles downloading and updating the app, under Google's privacy policy.

7. Ghost links

When you share a run as a link (“ghost”), the run (your steering inputs) is in the part of the link after the “#”. That part is never sent to our server. You decide whom you send the link to.

8. Deleting your account and data

To have your account and your progress in the cloud deleted, email privacy@wolsok.de with the subject “Bacteria Wars: delete account”. Give the email address of your Google account. A guest account has only a random identifier the game does not show, so we cannot link it to anyone (Art. 11 GDPR). To have a guest's progress deleted, first sign in with Google in the profile: the guest becomes your Google account, and we can find it. We delete the account and all its game data within 30 days and confirm the deletion to you. Delete the data on your device as described in section 3. Signing out alone deletes nothing.

9. Your rights

Under the GDPR you have the right to

  • access your data (Art. 15),
  • rectification (Art. 16) and erasure (Art. 17),
  • restriction of processing (Art. 18),
  • data portability (Art. 20),
  • object to processing based on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (Art. 21).

You may also complain to a data protection supervisory authority, for example the one where you live (Art. 77 GDPR).

10. Children

The game can be played without an account and without giving any personal details. Google's age rules apply to signing in with Google.

11. Changes

If the game changes to process other data, we update this policy. The version on this page applies.

result.output:
# Bacteria Wars for Android

The Android app of the bacteria game. It is a
[Trusted Web Activity](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/android/trusted-web-activity)
(TWA): a thin native shell that opens https://bacteria-wars.wolsok.de in
Chrome, fullscreen and without any browser UI. The game itself is the PWA
`bacteria-game-remote`, so every web deploy updates the app as well; only
changes to this folder need a new app release. Offline play, saves, sound and
haptics work as in the installed PWA.

What the shell adds:

- launcher icon (adaptive, with a monochrome layer for themed icons) and a
  splash screen, both drawn by `tools/bacteria-game/generate-icons.ts`
  (`npx nx run bacteria-game-remote:icons`)
- immersive mode, matching `"display": "fullscreen"` of the web manifest
- links to bacteria-wars.wolsok.de open in the app
- a WebView fallback for devices without a TWA-capable browser

## Build

Needs JDK 21 and the Android SDK (`ANDROID_HOME`, or `sdk.dir` in
`local.properties`). The Gradle wrapper downloads Gradle itself.

```bash
npx nx run bacteria-wars-android:apk               # debug APK
npx nx run bacteria-wars-android:apk:release       # release APK
npx nx run bacteria-wars-android:bundle            # release app bundle for Play
npx nx run bacteria-wars-android:lint-android      # Android lint
```

Outputs land in `app/build/outputs/`. Install a debug APK with
`adb install app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`.

The version comes from the workspace's `version.json`: 74.44.1 becomes
`versionName` 74.44.1 and `versionCode` 74044001.

The `Android app` GitHub workflow builds and lints the debug APK on every
change to this folder and keeps it as a workflow artifact, to try the app on a
phone. Each run signs it with a fresh debug key, so uninstall the previous one
before installing the next, and expect Chrome's URL bar on top: only keys
listed in `assetlinks.json` get fullscreen.

## Fullscreen needs Digital Asset Links

Chrome only hides its URL bar when the site and the app vouch for each other:

- the app names the site in its `asset_statements` (set in
  `app/build.gradle.kts`)
- the site names the app's package and the SHA-256 fingerprints of the keys it
  is signed with in
  `apps/bacteria-game-remote/src/.well-known/assetlinks.json`, deployed to
  `https://bacteria-wars.wolsok.de/.well-known/assetlinks.json`

Until a fingerprint is listed there, the app still runs, but Chrome shows a
URL bar on top of it. The Gradle build reads the package name from that file,
so it is the one place to change it.

## Releases and Google Play

The app ships with the workspace release, as an Nx `deploy` target like the
other apps. The `Deploy release` workflow runs `nx affected -t deploy` for
every release, in its own `android` leg that compares against the last
`*-android-deployed` tag. When a release touches this folder,
`nx run bacteria-wars-android:deploy` (`tools/bacteria-game/deploy-android.ts`):

1. builds the signed release APK and app bundle, with the version code of the
   release's `version.json`,
2. uploads the bundle to the **internal testing** track on Google Play,
3. attaches the APK and bundle to the GitHub release as
   `bacteria-wars-<tag>.apk` and `.aab`.

Promoting a build to production stays a step in the Play Console. A release
whose bundle is on Play already skips the upload, so a failed deploy can run
again (Actions → Deploy release → Run workflow, with the tag). Web changes do
not ship the app: the app shows the live site, so only changes here need a
new build.

### Store listing

The same deploy brings the Play store listing in line with `store/`:

- `store/listings/<language>/` holds `title.txt`, `short-description.txt`
  and `full-description.txt` for each language (Play takes 30, 80 and 4000
  characters),
- `store/graphics/` holds `icon.png`, `feature-graphic.png` and
  `screenshot-<n>.png`, the same for every language; the landscape
  screenshots serve phones and tablets alike.

Only what differs from Play is sent, images compared by their SHA-256, so an
unchanged listing goes to no review. Since the files sit in this project, a
change to them alone also makes the app affected and ships it with the next
release. The graphics come from the running game:

```bash
npx nx serve bacteria-game-remote                 # in one terminal
npx nx run bacteria-wars-android:store-assets     # in another
```

The matches are live, so every run draws slightly different screenshots:
commit the ones worth showing.

### Promo video

`store/promo-video/` holds the promo video, as `bacteria-wars-promo-<lang>-<format>.mp4`
(English and German 16:9, English 9:16), and `videos.json` with each one's
YouTube title, description, tags and privacy, and the Play listing it belongs
to. The deploy uploads every video whose file is not on the YouTube channel
yet (see `tools/youtube/README.md`) and sets it as the promo video of its
listing. Without the YouTube secrets it leaves the videos alone.

The videos come from the running game, like the graphics:

```bash
npx nx serve bacteria-game-remote                 # in one terminal
npx nx run bacteria-wars-android:promo-video     # in another
```

`tools/bacteria-game/promo-video/make.ts` plays four clips, records them with

I've added Buy Me a Coffee, Play Store tips and AdSense ads to Bacteria Wars, copying how movepath does it. It's in PR #2578: https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/pull/2578. CI on the first commit was green, including e2e and the Android build. CI is now running on the second commit, which has the review fixes. Locally the full suite (1123 game tests, 12 app tests), lint, the production build and the Android build plus lint all pass. I checked the Support tile and the coffee button in the browser at desktop and phone size.

**What players see:**
- **In the browser:** a **Support** tile in the main menu and a "Buy me a coffee" button on *How to play*, both going to `buymeacoffee.com/wolf`.
- **In the Android app:** the same tile opens a dialog with tip buttons (`tip_small`, `tip_medium`, `tip_large`) paid through Google Play. The app never shows the coffee link, because Play only allows tips through Play Billing.
- **Ads:** AdSense ads on the *How to play* and *Profile* screens, never during a match. They only show after the player has answered Google's consent banner, and *How to play* has an "Ad privacy settings" button to change that choice.
- **Inside the angular-examples site** the game shows neither tips nor ads, because that site has no consent banner.

**Privacy policy:** it no longer says "no ads". There are new German and English sections on ads, consent and tips, and the later sections are renumbered.

**Branch:** the work is on a new branch, `feat/bacteria-wars-support`, in a separate worktree at `~/repos/wol-sok-mono-support`. Your `feat/eu-central-1` checkout is untouched.

CodeRabbit and Codex were both rate-limited, so I ran `/code-review` and `/simplify` myself, as CLAUDE.md says. Three of the fixes mattered:
- **Telling the app from the browser:** the first version treated any visit opened from another Android app (Gmail, the Google app) as the Play app, which hid the coffee link. It also would have shown the coffee link inside the app on phones where it runs in a WebView. The app now launches with `?source=twa` and the game checks for that or our own package name.
- **Tips left half-finished** by a closed app are now cleared once billing has connected, so Play doesn't refund them.
- **Duplicate font loading:** the page loaded the fonts stylesheet twice; now it's one link.

I'll keep watching the PR and fix anything that turns red. Once CI is green I'll squash-merge it, as CLAUDE.md allows.

**What you need to do before it earns anything:**
1. **AdSense:**
   - Create a display ad unit and put it in `environment.prod.ts` as `support.ads` (the line is there as a comment). Until then no ad script and no consent banner load.
   - Make sure your Privacy & Messaging consent message covers `bacteria-wars.wolsok.de`.
   - Turn Auto ads off for that subdomain, or Google's own overlay ads would cover the game.
   - `wolsok.de/ads.txt` already covers the subdomain.
2. **Play Console:**
   - Create the three tips as consumable in-app products, with a payments profile.
   - Declare "Contains ads" and update the Data safety form.
   - Tips can only be tested on a phone, with a build from a Play testing track.
3. **Families policy:** if the game's Play target audience includes children, Play's rules for ads aimed at children apply. Check this before the ads go live.

I haven't been able to create the three tip products yet; it can't be done from here today. I pushed the setup that creates them automatically on the next Android release, which will be the release that ships this PR. It's commit `4afd3df7` on PR #2578; CI is running on it now.

**Why not now:**
- **No access from here:** your local gcloud login doesn't include access to the Google Play API. Play answered "insufficient authentication scopes". Only the deploy's service account (the `PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` GitHub secret) has that access.
- **Play would refuse:** Play only accepts in-app products once a bundle with the billing permission is on a track. The bundle on Play now doesn't have it; this PR adds it.

**What I pushed:**
- `apps/bacteria-wars-android/store/tips.json` lists the products, with German and English titles:

  | Product | Title (EN / DE) | Price in Germany |
  |---|---|---|
  | `tip_small` | Small coffee / Kleiner Kaffee | 2,99 € |
  | `tip_medium` | Large coffee / Großer Kaffee | 4,99 € |
  | `tip_large` | Coffee and cake / Kaffee mit Kuchen | 9,99 € |

  Play converts these prices for every other country.
- `tools/bacteria-game/play-tips.ts` creates or updates the products and activates them, modelled on movepath's `publish-play-tips`. The Android deploy runs it right after uploading the bundle.
- If creating the products fails (for example, no payments profile yet), the deploy finishes the release and store listing first and only then reports the error.
- Broken product texts stop the deploy before the build.

I checked the code against a fake Play API, which made the expected calls, and lint and type checks pass. It hasn't run against the real Play API yet; the first real run is that release.

**Two things only you can do in the Play Console, before that release:**
1. Link a payments profile; without one, Play rejects every in-app product.
2. Give the service account permission to manage in-app products (Users and permissions → the service account → app permissions).

If you'd rather create the products right away, you could log in locally with Play API access: `gcloud auth application-default login --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/androidpublisher,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`. Play would still refuse them until the billing bundle is on a track, though.
